records.title: Manchester International Airport Phase 2 - Platform Civils
records.description:
"The planned introduction of longer train services to the Airport in response to future demand growth will mean that double stacking arrangements of trains as currently used will no longer be viable. Through the project's Delivery Steering Group, Northern and TransPennine Express have carried out analysis which has identified that additional platform capacity is needed at the airport in order to realise the full benefit of longer train services serving the airport.
      
      The scheme is part of a package of proposed measures in the Manchester area that are being designed/planned to boost capacity and resilience, emanating from the Cross Manchester Capacity and Reliability Improvement Study. Improving the operation of train services in the centre of Manchester and providing further capacity at Manchester Airport station, aligns with the strategic aims of Network Rail, TfGM, TfN and the wider industry.  This project in in Tranche 1 of the Manchester and North West Transformation Programme (MNTP):
       
      A remodelling of the station at Manchester Airport, specifically a platform addition or extension of multiple platforms, or provision of a new turnback facility, will be essential to accommodate the planned implementation of longer rolling stock services.
           
      The redevelopment of these platforms will enable permissive working of two 6x24m (144m) trains, in two of the four platforms at the Airport Station. This will allow for the unaltered retention of all existing TOC services both originating and terminating at the Airport Station under 'double-stacking' conditions.

records.title: Lower Cambourne Playpark works
records.description:
Introduction
Cambourne Town Council ("the Council") wishes to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced Contractor to undertake refurbishment works at the Lower Cambourne Play Area.
Prospective Contractors are invited to submit a quotation to meet the Council's requirements as set out within this document and the accompanying play park upgrade brief.

2. Project Overview
The Council is seeking to upgrade the Lower Cambourne Play Area to provide:
•	Improved infrastructure
•	Enhanced and modernised play equipment
•	Increased play value and opportunities
The Council has allocated funding as part of its commitment to improving the health and wellbeing of residents.
The appointed Contractor will be expected to work collaboratively with the Council to deliver a high-quality, inclusive, and engaging play space.


3. Design Principles
Inclusivity and accessibility are central to the Council's objectives. The Contractor must demonstrate:
•	Experience in delivering inclusive and accessible play environments
•	Consideration of a wide range of ages and abilities
•	Innovative design solutions that maximise play value
A meeting prior tender submission is crucial to ensure that the Councils vision for this play park is understood. Please contact Clerk@cambournetowncouncil.gov.uk 

4. Scope of Works
The works will include (but are not limited to):
•	Design and installation of new play equipment
•	Landscaping and associated infrastructure works
•	Removal and safe disposal of all existing play equipment and associated services
•	Recycling and reuse of materials where practicable, including potential relocation of serviceable equipment to alternative sites (subject to agreement with the Council)

5. Community Engagement
The Contractor will be required to support public consultation as part of the design process:
•	Two public consultation events shall be held:
o	One following the development of the initial design proposal
o	A second follow-up consultation, if required, to incorporate and respond to public feedback and any proposed amendments

6. Programme
Estimated contract dates:
•	Anticipated start: Late May 2026
•	Duration: Approximately 2 months
•	Completion: Prior to the start of the Summer Holidays 2026
The contract will include a 12-month defects liability period following completion.

7. Tender Documentation
This document should be read in conjunction with:
•	Material considerations
•	Accessibility Statement



10. Submission Details
Submission Deadline:
•	15th May 2026 at 9:00am
Submission Method:
•	Tenders must be submitted electronically via email to:
clerk@cambournetowncouncil.gov.uk
Late submissions may not be considered.

11. Additional Requirements
Contractors should demonstrate:
•	Relevant experience in similar play park projects
•	Ability to deliver within programme and budget
•	Commitment to sustainability and waste minimisation
•	Strong approach to health and safety compliance

records.title: CA18704 - St Matthew's Primary School _ Luton
records.description:
St Matthew's Primary School is seeking an experienced, innovative, and customer-focused catering partner to deliver high-quality school meal services for our pupils and staff.
Located in the heart of Luton's historic Old Town, St Matthew's is a large and vibrant primary school with a diverse school community. We are committed to providing nutritious, enjoyable, and well-presented meals that support the health, wellbeing, and educational success of our pupils.
We are inviting expressions of interest from catering providers who can demonstrate:
•	A strong track record of delivering successful school catering services.
•	Commitment to providing fresh, nutritious, and balanced meals that meet or exceed School Food Standards.
•	Innovative menu development that reflects the diversity of our school community and promotes healthy eating.
•	Excellent customer service and engagement with pupils, staff, parents, and school leadership.
•	Effective management of kitchen operations, staffing, food safety, and compliance requirements.
•	Initiatives to increase meal uptake, particularly for Universal and Free School Meals.
•	A commitment to sustainability, waste reduction, and responsible sourcing.
The successful contractor will work in partnership with the school to create a positive dining experience, encourage healthy lifestyle choices, and support the wider educational objectives of the school.
Suppliers interested in this opportunity will be expected to demonstrate financial stability, relevant experience within the education sector, robust safeguarding practices, and the capability to deliver a high-quality catering service throughout the contract term.
St Matthew's Primary School looks forward to engaging with suppliers who share our vision of delivering exceptional food and service to our school community.

Not registered:

records.title: CA18703 - Barwell Infant School _ Leicester
records.description:
Barwell Infant School is seeking a catering partner who can deliver fresh, nutritious, and appealing meals that children genuinely want to eat. We believe that food is a fundamental part of the school day-supporting wellbeing, fuelling learning, and helping pupils develop healthy habits that last far beyond their time with us.
The ideal partner will act with honesty, integrity, and a clear commitment to putting pupils at the centre of every decision. From menu design to service style, we expect a caterer who consistently asks, "What is best for the children?" and demonstrates this through their actions, communication, and daily practice.
Lunchtimes at Barwell Infant School must be enjoyable, vibrant, and inclusive. We want a dining experience that feels warm and welcoming, where pupils are encouraged to try new foods, feel confident in their choices, and look forward to their meal each day. The right partner will bring creativity, professionalism, and a genuine passion for feeding young people well.
A key indicator of operational success will be increased meal uptake. Growth in participation will reflect not only the quality of the food, but the strength of the service, the engagement with pupils and families, and the overall dining experience delivered.
Barwell Infant School is committed to forming a collaborative, long term partnership with a caterer who shares our values and our ambition to provide an exceptional meal service for every child.

records.title: Provision of UPS - MEICA-UPS-01
records.description:
The Subcontractor shall design, manufacture, supply, deliver, test and commission 4 No. complete UPS systems: 1 No. at Stoneleigh, 1 No. at Canley Brook and 2 No. at Burton Green.

1. Technical Requirements
Each UPS shall be rated at 210 kVA, 400 V, with 4 x 60 kW power modules and N+1 hot-swappable architecture. The Subcontractor shall demonstrate that the required connected load remains supported with one power module unavailable.
Requirement Stoneleigh Canley Brook Burton Green
Battery sizing load 35 kW 17 kW 70 kW
Connected design load 31 kW TBC 66 kW
Protection breaker 100 A 100 A 250 A
Separate static switch N/A N/A 400 A, 400 V

Each UPS shall provide an output fault current of 987 A for 200 ms. Supplier submissions shall demonstrate compatibility with the project protection requirements.

2. Batteries
Provide complete VRLA battery systems, including racks/enclosures, interconnections, isolation and protection, delivering 90 minutes' autonomy at the specified battery sizing load. Batteries shall recharge to 95% within 900 minutes. Submit sizing and recharge calculations.

3. Transformers and Ancillary Equipment
Provide 250 kVA, 1:1, Dzn0 input and output isolation transformers, together with ATS, static switching and external maintenance bypass arrangements required by the approved site-specific drawings. ATS shall be 400 A, four-pole where indicated.

Include all interconnecting cables, battery cables, protective devices and terminations identified as the UPS supplier's responsibility. Coordinate interfaces with incoming supplies and UPS switchboards.

4. Monitoring
Provide BMS interfaces for battery DC voltage, charge percentage, battery alarms/faults and charger status/alarms. Include communications protocols, interface hardware and point schedules for the UPS, ATS and UPS switchboard, with interface testing.

5. Delivery and Coordination
Scheduled UPS cabinet dimensions are 1,200 W x  1,996 H x 1,100 D mm. Confirm complete equipment footprints, weights, clearances and delivery requirements before manufacture.

6. Testing and Handover
Include FAT, commissioning, SAT and resistive load bank testing, with all temporary equipment, connections and removal. Demonstrate capacity, autonomy, recharge, redundancy, transfer/bypass operation, alarms and communications. Provide evidence of fault-current performance.

Submit equipment drawings, schematics, protection data, test procedures/results, commissioning records, as-built information and O&M manuals.

Suppliers shall identify proposed equipment and deviations. Confirm the missing Canley Brook design load, whether Burton Green loads apply per UPS, and site-specific equipment quantities and supply boundaries before manufacture.

This contract is to provide specialist analytical support to strengthen National Highways' approach to achieving its RIS3 road safety targets. Current forecasts indicate a material gap against the ambitious safety outcomes set for the road period, and there is a need for a robust, evidence-based understanding of which interventions will have the greatest impact on reducing casualties and delivering value for money.

The objective is to develop a prioritised programme of road safety interventions supported by clear evidence of effectiveness, costs and benefits, including metrics such as cost per KSI prevented.

records.description:
ONR invited proposals to provide our service requirements from suppliers appointed to the Crown Commercial Services Framework, RM6309 Management Consultancy Framework Four - Lot 2 (Strategy and Policy).

BACKGROUND TO THE PROJECT

The Office for Nuclear Regulation (ONR) is committed to strengthening its position as a modern, high performing, and values driven regulator. To support this ambition, ONR intends to commission a comprehensive cultural climate assessment.

This requirement aligns with ONR's 2030 Strategy and responds to expectations set out in the UK Government Review of Nuclear Regulation. It is intended to reinforce ONR's cultural foundations and ensure that organisational behaviours, leadership practices and working environments are aligned to strategic objectives.

ONR recognises that organisational culture is dynamic and continually evolving. Senior leadership plays a critical role in shaping culture through decision making, behaviours and the environment created across the organisation. As such, cultural improvement must address both:
•	Structural factors (e.g. governance, organisational design); and
•	Infrastructure factors (e.g. leadership behaviours, decision making norms, psychological environment).

Our current bi-annual survey is exceptionally strong at measuring employee    sentiment, psychological safety, and leadership role-modelling. It tells us how our people experience the workplace. However, it does not measure our collective capacity to deliver on our mission.

The assessment will provide an evidence based view of ONR's current cultural climate, building on previous work including the Alliance Manchester Business School (AMBS) survey undertaken approximately three years ago, and supporting ongoing commitments with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).

records.title: Homes England - Wider Industry Survey
records.description:
Homes England is seeking a supplier to design and deliver an industry survey for Homes England and the National Housing Bank (NHB). The research will explore why organisations in the sector may not currently engage, where there may be opportunities to develop new partnerships, and critically, the future collaborations and initiatives that could be introduced to support delivery of the regeneration and growth agenda both regionally and nationally.\r
\r
The core objective of this research is to address a current evidence gap by exploring barriers to engagement and the factors that influence partnership working - both for Homes England and the NHB. Findings will be used to:\r
\r
1) Support more targeted market engagement and better-informed strategic decision-making as a result.\r
2) Inform the future development of NHB products and services, to support growth and wider investment priorities.\r
\r
The supplier will be required to support stakeholder mapping, identify and agree the target sample, design and deliver a quantitative and qualitative survey, and provide analysis and recommendations. The target audience will include eligible organisations from within the sector that have encountered barriers to engagement and /or have had a limited experience to date due to the perceived relevance of the service offer. Within these identified groups, the research will focus particularly on organisations that may have the potential to become future partners of Homes England or the NHB.\r
\r
Awarded using GCA's Research and Insight DPS.

records.title: Provision of BMS System MEICA-BMS-01
records.description:
The scope of works includes a two-stage delivery approach covering the complete design, supply, configuration, integration, testing and installation of the Building Management System for Canley Brook, Burton Green and Stoneleigh Pumping Stations under the HS2 N1/N2 MEICA works. 
      
      The centralised system at each location shall comprise of a dedicated BMS panel with dual-redundant PLCs, HMIs, remote interface enclosures and a dedicated BMS LAN, and distributed interface enclosures located within the relevant plant rooms to facilitate communications between plant systems and provide connectivity to the HS2 Network Integrated Control Centre (NICC).
      
      The BMS shall integrate the mechanical and electrical building services, providing monitoring, control, alarm management, and operator interfaces for the pumping stations and portal building. The system shall be designed in accordance with the project control strategy and applicable HS2 technical standards while coordinating with interfacing subcontractors to ensure seamless integration of all connected systems.
      
      The proposed BMS shall provide monitoring, control, alarms and graphical visualisation for HVAC, LV distribution and metering, UPS, lighting, fire alarms, public health services, pumped drainage and disabled toilet alarms. The scope also includes reviewing design inputs, updating the Functional Design Specification and generic drawings, and coordinating all interfaces required for full mechanical and electrical system integration. Sella Controls will also assess the cyber security risks associated with the BMS system.

Additional information: Please review the Scope of work and drawings for the works.

records.title: SZC CWA - Pool Bunker Construction
records.description:
The contract will deliver a commissioned, weathertight and operational Pool Bunker above the base slab. The facility will support assembly, welding and inspection activities before modules are transferred to the Nuclear Island.
      
      The scope of works includes:
      •	Primary steel frame and crane runway beams. 
      •	Rainscreen cladding and industrial doors, with precast cladding retained as the alternative envelope. 
      •	Five-section retractable roof. 
      •	Secondary steelwork platforms, working levels and access arrangements. 
      •	Mechanical, electrical and public health services, including local exhaust ventilation, power, lighting and controls. 
      •	Passenger and goods hoists, stair cores and roof access. 
      •	Installation and commissioning of three free-issued gantry cranes. 
      •	Tented workshop, lightning protection and earthing. 
      •	Testing, commissioning, quality records and formal handover. 
      
      The base slab and the separate site non-destructive testing contract are outside this sourcing strategy. Their interfaces will be defined in the tender documents and managed through the contract programme.
      
      The key scope deliverables are:
      •	Completed design to RIBA stage 4 and coordinated construction information. 
      •	Approved contractor programme aligned to project milestones. 
      •	Constructed and commissioned Pool Bunker, including roof, cranes, platforms, access and building services. 
      •	Completed health, safety, quality and assurance records. 
      •	Demonstrated interfaces with the base slab, utilities and non-destructive testing arrangements. 
      •	Formal handover following operational readiness review.
      
      The timescales are as follows:
      
      The Pool Bunker is required to support the planned assembly, welding and inspection of pool and tank liner modules before transfer to the Nuclear Island. The current estimated site construction period is:
      •	40 weeks for the preferred rainscreen and Safe RAD solution.
      •	46 weeks for the 275 mm precast fallback solution.
      
      The current target is for the Pool Bunker to be completed and handed over by 28 February 2028, ready to support the planned assembly, welding and inspection of pool and tank liner modules. The programme is dependent on completion of the base slab and availability of the K10 area and will be revalidated once the K10 release date is confirmed.

records.title: Preliminary Market Engagement: Development of Digital Training Materials on Foreign Interference Risks in Higher Education
records.description:
The Authority is seeking market engagement with organisations that have experience in designing and delivering digital learning products, training content, and educational resources for the higher education (HE) sector.

Background

The Authority is exploring options for the development of a suite of digital training materials aimed at supporting staff within UK higher education providers to better understand, identify and manage foreign interference risks.

The training package will support awareness and understanding of:

Foreign interference risks and how they may manifest within the higher education sector.
Relevant legal, regulatory and policy frameworks.
Practical considerations for academics, managers and governance professionals.
Good practice approaches to risk management and decision-making within institutional settings.

The training materials should support staff in making robust, informed decisions that align with institutional policies, risk management frameworks, and applicable higher education and national security legislation and regulations.

Scope of Requirement

The Authority is seeking views from the market on the design, development and delivery of a digital learning package which may include:

Interactive e-learning modules.
Scenario-based learning and case studies.
Knowledge assessments and learning checks.
Supporting guidance materials and resources.
Accessible content suitable for a range of higher education audiences.

The final product should complement and align with existing sector resources relating to Trusted Research, Research Security and the management of international risks in higher education.

Relevant resources include:

Protecting UK Higher Education from Foreign Interference
Managing Risks in Internationalisation: Security Related Issues
Managing Risk in International Education Partnerships and Overseas Operations
Intended Audience

The proposed training package is expected to support:

Academic staff, particularly those working in disciplines or activities that may be exposed to foreign interference risks.
Student services managers.
Professional services staff with responsibility for governance, compliance, risk management and institutional assurance.
Senior leaders and decision-makers.
Members and Chairs of Governing Bodies.

Important Information

This notice is issued solely for the purposes of market engagement and information gathering. It does not constitute the commencement of a procurement process and does not commit the Authority to undertake any procurement exercise. Any future procurement opportunity will be advertised separately in accordance with applicable procurement requirements.

It is also important to note that should a procurement be undertaken the planned route to market would be using GCA DPS  RM6129 so potential suppliers should be registered for this DPS.

records.title: S30168 Feasibility study for developing a quality measure for variable signs and signals settings
records.description: Timeliness of variable signs and signals (VSS) settings is one of our company's performance indicators. However, we're not able to evaluate the quality of these settings, whether they're appropriate and beneficial for those using our roads. These factors drive customer trust and satisfaction and influence both the Strategic Roads User Survey (SRUS) and Average Delay Key Performance Indicator scores. A KPMG review of our SRUS performance recommended measuring the quality of VSS settings to help identify how we can improve scores. As part of our CSC Business Plan requirement to improve customer experience through better in-journey information we want to commit £83,289.85 of funding (approved through a portfolio business case for VSS improvements by CSC IDC) to carry out a feasibility study to explore the potential of developing a VSS quality measure that would give us sight of how well we're doing in this area. This work is part of the Customer Service Development Group's ongoing portfolio of VSS improvements which seek to improve customer experience and contribute to an increase in customer satisfaction scores. In the 2025-26 reporting year SRUS recorded 71% overall satisfaction and 69% for information on electronic signs. The RIS3 KPI requires SRUS scores to improve year-on-year. Any proposed measure should aim at helping us to identify where changes can improve satisfaction scores. We anticipate the feasibility study will require engagement with National Highways' teams to draw expertise and input on the potential of existing system and process outputs to be used to assess the quality of settings made. Therefore, some travel may be required. National Highways will facilitate the consultant's access to contributing teams. This feasibility study involves no additional IT or resource requirements.

records.title: Testing the effect of behavioural interventions on agri-environment scheme optio
records.description:
Testing the effect of behavioural interventions on agri-environment scheme option selection

This project follows a series of Choice Architecture Tests (CATs) that have been commissioned by Defra's Farming Directorate Behavioural Science and Analytics team. These CATs have tested various interventions in a hypothetical agri-environment scheme application environment to understand their effect on option selection. Key findings include:

• CAT 1 : tested the effect of defaults (pre-selected actions) on a hypothetical Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) application. Results showed a statistically significant increase in the environmental quality of the agreement generated through defaults compared to the current SFI application design.
• CAT 2 : tested the effect of defaults and guided selection on a hypothetical Countryside Stewardship (CS) mid-tier application. Results for CAT 2 also showed defaults being effective. Compared to the current CS mid-tier design & some aspects of guided selection tested during the experiment, defaults led to more spatially targeted actions being chosen (the primary outcome of the experiment) by farmers, which might indicate higher quality environmental agreements.
• CAT 3 : tested the effect of geospatial functionality (presenting guidance on spatial priorities visually) and offering a default totaliser (that shows the potential financial reward for choosing options) on a hypothetical SFI application. The study found no evidence that the tool changed the mean number of spatial priorities per action selected. The tool significantly reduced the total number of actions selected.
• CAT 4 : used qualitative methods to test the effect of offering defaults with farmers who find it difficult to access and use digital tools and services, (i.e. those with low 'digital literacy'), to assess whether findings from CAT 1 & CAT 2 are consistent for these farmers. The major barriers to using digital technology were confidence, time and motivation, though barriers to applying for ELM schemes independently were not primarily related to digital skills. Defaults were not viewed positively but highlighting and the review page were.
• CAT 5 : tested the effect of "Object Oriented" (OO) framing, which categorises information by tangible, real-life objects aligned with farmers' mental models, on finding and understanding of regulatory information. Overall, OO framing did not significantly improve navigation and understanding.
